q: The Cahn-Hilliard equation uₜ = −Δ(Δu − f(u)) models phase separation. It differs from the Allen-Cahn equation (uₜ = Δu − f(u)) in that the Cahn-Hilliard is:
opts: A conservation law (∫u dx is preserved) while Allen-Cahn is not mass-conserving
exp: Cahn-Hilliard conserves mass: ∫_Ω u dx = const (it's in conservation form uₜ = −∇·J). Allen-Cahn does not conserve mass (∫u changes in time). Both decrease the free energy ∫(½|∇u|² + F(u))dx, but via different mechanisms (H^{-1} vs L² gradient flow).
